extracted.intended_audience: college administrators, grants officers, and higher-education faculty interested in promoting faculty grantsmanship
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of barriers, motivators, and institutional practices that affect faculty involvement in grant seeking and grant writing in campus-based state colleges, with recommendations for administrative actions to increase faculty grantsmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Released time to work on successful grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of released time from regular duties to work on awarded grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents rated released time to work on successful grants as highly important (89% rated released time to work on successful grants 'very important' or 'important'); 44% reported their colleges provided released time 'very often' or 'often'. Recommendation: provide released time for awarded grants to demonstrate institutional commitment and enable sustained research activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Released time to prepare a proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of released time specifically to prepare grant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very few respondents reported released time to prepare proposals (5% 'often'; 0% 'very often'), yet 74% rated released time to prepare a proposal 'very important' or 'important'. Recommendation: institutions should provide limited released time or awards to enable speculative proposal development and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration in tenure and promotion decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Weight given to grant-related activities in promotion and tenure evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration in tenure and promotion was reported as provided 'very often' or 'often' by 41% of respondents and rated 'very important' or 'important' by 77%. Recommendation: explicitly incorporate grants/sponsored research as valued scholarly activity in promotion/tenure criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition in college publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Public recognition of faculty grant activity in campus publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition in college publications was the most frequently reported reward (61% 'very often' or 'often'). Recommendation: use college newspapers, alumni bulletins, and official communications to publicize proposals and awards; send acknowledgement and congratulations letters from administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other forms of public recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-publication recognition such as awards, ceremonies, or personal acknowledgement by leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents valued public recognition; recommendations include letters from the president/provost, personal calls, and annual awards (e.g., 'research award of the year') to create a climate that values grant activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel support (secretarial help or graduate assistants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing clerical or graduate-student assistance to faculty engaged in grant activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a minority reported frequent provision (11% reported 'very often' or 'often' receiving extra secretarial help), yet 74% rated personnel support 'very important' or 'important'. Recommendation: provide extra clerical help or graduate assistants to active grant writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support (extra college funds for travel or equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing institutional funds for travel, equipment, or other administrative support related to grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 15% reported frequent provision; 77% rated it important. Recommendation: allocate modest discretionary funds to support grant development and grant-related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return to department of a portion of indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reallocating a portion of grant indirect/administrative costs back to the academic department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported infrequently (4% 'very often' or 'often'), but those who receive such returns view them as motivating. Recommendation: consider sharing indirect costs with departments to support travel, equipment, or replacing faculty teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal financial compensation / modest stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary rewards (small stipends) for successful grants or published works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author recommends modest stipends (e.g., $25–$50) funded by institutional foundations as inexpensive ways to show appreciation; this is a low-cost tangible reward to value scholarly activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional awards (e.g., 'research award of the year')
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual or periodic non-cash awards recognizing outstanding faculty scholarly activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to create peer-judged awards at school or institution level to publicly recognize research/grant accomplishments and build morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functioning grants or sponsored research office
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating centralized office to support grants and sponsored research on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eighty percent reported having a grants office; campuses with functioning offices reported significantly more technical assistance and better outcomes. Recommendation: create an office if none exists; it should be more than a processing unit—actively assist faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants office staffed with grant writing specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants office personnel should include grant writing specialists willing to help find sponsors and assist with proposal drafting and editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: grants offices should 'roll up their sleeves' to help faculty identify sponsors, edit sections, and develop proposals. This hands-on support reduces intimidation and increases success rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty handbook/manual for grants and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive handbook outlining policies, procedures, responsibilities, and administrative processes for grants and contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should include policies on contact with sponsors, proposal and budget preparation, approvals, duties of PIs, negotiators, negotiating/signing authority, patents, human/animal subjects protection, ownership rights, facilities. Recommendation: distribute to new faculty at orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive technical assistance and training (workshops/seminars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering workshops, seminars, and individualized assistance in grant development at varied times/locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field seminars and individual assistance remove intimidation (Lischwe). Recommendation: offer sessions repeatedly, at accessible times, and target female and junior faculty who report greater need/importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined campus proposal approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplifying internal approval/signature requirements to speed proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine required signatories (department chair, dean, personnel, budget, grants officer, VP, president) and eliminate unnecessary steps while preserving integrity. Recommendation: reduce bottlenecks to improve timeliness for competitive proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide tangible rewards (e.g., released time, return of indirect costs, funds for adjuncts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional commitment to tangible incentives to encourage faculty grant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include limited released time to prepare proposals, reallocation of indirect costs to departments, establishing research funds to pay adjuncts who replace released-time faculty, and modest stipends for awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate indirect costs to departments / establish a research fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Using indirect cost returns to support departmental research activities or to fund adjunct replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: reallocate a percentage of indirects to departments or create a fund to pay adjuncts, enabling departments to support released-time faculty without harming instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote collegial collaboration and student involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate faculty-to-faculty and faculty-student teaming for grant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: grants administrators should survey faculty interests and bring individuals together to respond to RFPs or develop speculative proposals; encourage collegial work and student involvement as a motivator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent administrative communication valuing grant development
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular, visible administrative messages that institutional leadership values sponsored research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: send acknowledgement/congratulation letters, publicize grants in campus media, have leaders personally congratulate successful grantees to signal institutional value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add grant development instruction to graduate curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer a course in grant development for graduate students to prepare future faculty in grantsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: include grant development in graduate training so potential future faculty learn to seek funding and write competitive grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of grant opportunity information
rubrics_metrics.description: Active distribution of information about available funding opportunities to faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified in literature (Bergen) as a 'seed activity' necessary to enhance the grants climate. Recommendation: proactively disseminate timely funding notices to faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative commitment and presidential support
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong, sustained commitment from institutional leadership (including the president) to support grants activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Young and others found presidential commitment correlated with grant success; recommendation: leadership should visibly endorse and resource grantsmanship efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly defined institutional plans and objectives related to research
rubrics_metrics.description: Having explicit institutional research/goals and plans that align with grant-seeking activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a factor associated with successful federal grants; institutions should define objectives that guide faculty proposals and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-conceived and well-prepared proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that are clearly articulated, targeted to appropriate sponsors, and carefully prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Young and other literature emphasize proposal quality as critical to success. Recommendation: provide editorial and conceptual assistance to strengthen proposals; avoid shotgun, hastily-prepared submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance in proposal development (editing/critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hands-on administrative help to develop, edit, and critique proposal sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiedler and Lischwe found assistance and seminars reduce intimidation; recommendation: provide individualized editing and critique services as part of grants office functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help in how to look for grant opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and assistance on strategies and resources for finding suitable grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 34% reported receiving this help 'very often' or 'often', while 84% rated it 'very important' or 'important'. Recommendation: proactively teach searching strategies and maintain curated opportunity lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help in how to write competitive proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction and hands-on support in writing proposals that meet sponsor expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 15% reported frequent help, but 82% rated it important. Recommendation: offer writing workshops, templates, and one-on-one coaching to raise competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help in how to prepare accurate and adequate budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance in budget preparation to ensure realistic, fundable cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 14% received frequent help, while 80% rated it important. Recommendation: provide budgeting templates, training, and direct assistance (including negotiation guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Help in obtaining necessary administrative approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and assistance navigating campus approval/signature processes for proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 25% reported frequent help; 77% rated it important. Recommendation: grants office should assist in routing approvals and clarifying signatory requirements to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help in dealing with prospective sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance in interactions with potential funders, including negotiations and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 11% reported frequent help, but 77% rated it important. Recommendation: provide training and administrative backing when negotiating with sponsors to reduce novice anxiety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help in dealing with the college business office
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance coordinating with institutional fiscal offices on grant accounting and post-award administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 17% reported frequent help; 72% rated it important. Recommendation: facilitate liaison between faculty and business office; provide clear guidance on post-award procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance warning / timely information about funding deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness of receiving funding notices and advance warning to permit preparation of competitive proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of advance warning was cited by 40% as preventing competitive proposals. Recommendation: provide early notices and reasonable internal deadlines to allow quality proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy teaching and advising loads as obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which high instructional and advising responsibilities prevent faculty from pursuing grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overwhelming majority (89%) reported heavy teaching loads as 'very much' or 'much' impediment. Recommendation: provide released time or adjunct coverage to reduce load for active grant-seekers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee assignments / other departmental assignments as obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative and committee responsibilities that reduce faculty time for grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee assignments and other departmental duties were reported as substantial obstacles (43% and 42% respectively 'very much' or 'much'). Recommendation: consider workload adjustments for grant-active faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other scholarly or entrepreneurial interests competing for time
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty engagement in other scholarly activities that compete with grantsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 47% reported other scholarly/entrepreneurial interests as 'very much' or 'much' impediment. Recommendation: recognize faculty have competing priorities and offer incentives to re-balance time where institutional goals prioritize grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge about funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty unfamiliarity with where to find appropriate sponsors and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 32% identified lack of knowledge as an obstacle; literature (Daniels & Gallaher) cites it as a key barrier. Recommendation: provide curated funding databases, training, and individualized matching services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of training in grant seeking or grant writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient formal training in the mechanics and craft of grantsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 31% reported lack of training as an obstacle; active faculty perceived training deficits less often. Recommendation: offer structured training programs, mentoring, and seminars targeted especially to junior faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge of budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate skills in preparing accurate and defensible budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28% indicated budgeting knowledge as an obstacle; 80% rated budget assistance important. Recommendation: provide budget training and hands-on assistance in budget preparation and negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No colleagues with whom to work (lack of collaborators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation or lack of potential co-investigators decreases likelihood of pursuing proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28% cited lack of colleagues as an obstacle. Recommendation: facilitate faculty networking, thematic interest groups, and collaboration-matching efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumbersome sponsor regulations and campus review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex external sponsor rules and internal campus procedures that deter faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumbersome sponsor regulations (17%) and campus review/approval burdens were identified obstacles. Recommendation: provide clear guidance, training, and administrative assistance to navigate regulations and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived lack of a clearly defined system of rewards for obtaining external funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of transparent reward systems for faculty who secure external grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daniels & Gallaher identified lack of rewards systems as a barrier. Recommendation: develop and communicate clear tangible/intangible reward policies (released time, recognition, stipend, indirect returns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty cultural attitudes against grantsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty self-identification primarily as teachers and skepticism about pursuing grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some faculty consciously spurn grants and see them as poor institutional priorities; recognition that some will not seek grants under any conditions. Recommendation: communicate institutional value of scholarship but accept that grantsmanship may not appeal to all faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted support for junior faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of additional technical assistance and mentoring for junior or less-experienced faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study found junior faculty received technical assistance less frequently; recommendation: proactively offer targeted assistance to junior/non-tenured faculty while acknowledging competing teaching-development needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted support for female faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and address that female faculty place greater importance on technical assistance and may need tailored outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Females were more likely to stress importance of technical assistance across categories. Recommendation: ensure training and support are accessible and responsive to female faculty needs to help close perceived gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seed activities to enhance research/grants climate
rubrics_metrics.description: Early-stage activities (dissemination of opportunities, assistance in proposal development) that create a supportive environment for grant-seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergen noted these activities are necessary even if not directly correlated with success. Recommendation: invest in seed activities to build long-term grants culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear procedural information about sponsor availability and campus processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing faculty with procedural guidance on where to find funding and how campus processes work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many studies (Young, Daniels & Gallaher) cite lack of procedural information as a barrier. Recommendation: publish clear guides, create a handbook, and have grants staff assist in procedural matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate institutional staffing and financial support for grants work
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient institutional human and financial resources devoted to supporting grant development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of staff, financial support, and inadequate overhead were cited as reasons for institutional failure to obtain grants. Recommendation: invest in grants office staffing and modest seed funds to support faculty efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely proactive outreach and multiple scheduling of training
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering the same workshops/seminars at many times/locations to increase accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: accommodate faculty schedules by repeating sessions and offering them at accessible times/locations to maximize participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage high-quality matching of project to sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeting proposals to appropriate sponsors rather than shotgun submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hastily prepared or shotgun submissions are less likely to be funded; recommendation: teach sponsor-targeting strategies and provide editorial assistance to improve fit and competitiveness.
